result.topic_en: Euler substitutes fractions for the letters α, β, γ, … in an earlier theorem to get a general continued-fraction expansion of a series in powers of x/y (Theorem V), then begins Problem III, converting the series 1/α − 1/αβ + 1/αβγ − … into a continued fraction.

§. 37. Quod si in casu Theorematis loco litterarum $\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta$, etc. scribamus fractiones
$\frac{\alpha}{a}, \frac{\beta}{b}, \frac{\gamma}{c}, \frac{\delta}{d}$, etc.
vt habeamus hanc seriem:
$s=\frac{ax}{\alpha y}-\frac{bxx}{\beta yy}+\frac{cx^3}{\gamma y^3}-\frac{dx^4}{\delta y^4}+\text{etc.}$
fractio continua hinc formata ita se habebit:
$\frac{x}{s}=\frac{\alpha}{a}y+\cfrac{\alpha\alpha xy:aa}{\frac{\beta}{b}y-\frac{\alpha}{a}x+\cfrac{\beta\beta xy:bb}{\frac{\gamma}{c}y-\frac{\beta}{b}x+\cfrac{\gamma\gamma xy:cc}{\frac{\delta}{d}y-\frac{\gamma}{c}x+\text{etc.}}}}$
Hic iam primo vtrinque multiplicetur per $a$, deinde primae fractionis numerator et denominator multiplicentur per $ab$, secundae per $bc$, tertiae per $cd$, etc. et fractio continua hanc induet formam:
$\frac{ax}{s}=\alpha y+\cfrac{\alpha\alpha bxy}{a\beta y-\alpha bx+\cfrac{\beta\beta acxy}{b\gamma y-c\beta x+\cfrac{\gamma\gamma bdxy}{c\delta y-d\gamma x+\text{etc.}}}}$
vnde operae pretium erit sequens apponere

Theorema V.
§. 38. Si proposita fuerit series infinita huius formae:
$s=\frac{ax}{\alpha y}-\frac{bxx}{\beta yy}+\frac{cx^3}{\gamma y^3}-\frac{dx^4}{\delta y^4}+\text{etc.}$
inde formabitur sequens fractio continua:
$\frac{ax}{s}=\alpha y+\cfrac{\alpha\alpha bxy}{a\beta y-\alpha bx+\cfrac{\beta\beta acxy}{b\gamma y-c\beta x+\cfrac{\gamma\gamma bdxy}{c\delta y-d\gamma x+\text{etc.}}}}$

Problema III.
Propositam hanc seriem infinitam:
$s=\frac{1}{\alpha}-\frac{1}{\alpha\beta}+\frac{1}{\alpha\beta\gamma}-\frac{1}{\alpha\beta\gamma\delta}+\text{etc.}$
in fractionem continuam conuertere.

Solutio.
§. 39. Ex serie proposita formemus sequentes series:
$t=\frac{1}{\beta}-\frac{1}{\beta\gamma}+\frac{1}{\beta\gamma\delta}-\frac{1}{\beta\gamma\delta\epsilon}+\text{etc.}$,
$u=\frac{1}{\gamma}-\frac{1}{\gamma\delta}+\frac{1}{\gamma\delta\epsilon}-\frac{1}{\gamma\delta\epsilon\zeta}+\text{etc.}$
atque habebimus
$s=\frac{1-t}{\alpha},\ t=\frac{1-u}{\beta},\ u=\frac{1-v}{\gamma}$ etc.
hinc igitur deducimus
$\frac{1}{s}=\frac{\alpha}{1-t}=\alpha+\frac{\alpha t}{1-t}=\alpha+\frac{\alpha}{-1+\frac{1}{t}}$.

items.english: If an infinite series of this form is proposed: s = ax/(αy) − bx²/(βy²) + cx³/(γy³) − dx⁴/(δy⁴) + etc., then the following continued fraction is formed from it.

items.quote:

in fractionem continuam conuertere.
items.english: To convert this proposed infinite series, s = 1/α − 1/(αβ) + 1/(αβγ) − 1/(αβγδ) + etc., into a continued fraction.
